chapters.title: Language Movement & Rise of Bengali Nationalism (1947–1954)

content.overview: Partition of 1947, emergence of Pakistan, language controversy, 21st February 1952 sacrifices, Shaheed Minar, United Front Election of 1954 and 21-point charter.
key_terms: 21 February 1952: Martyrs Salam, Barkat, Rafiq, Jabbar, Shafiur sacrificed their lives for Bangla.
UNESCO Recognition: 21st February declared International Mother Language Day in 1999.
study_notes: Tamaddun Majlish was established on 1 September 1947 by Prof. Abul Kashem.
United Front (Jukta Front) won a landslide victory in the 1954 East Bengal election.

mcqs.content: Which cultural organization initiated the movement for Bengali as a state language in September 1947? A. Chhayanaut B. Tamaddun Majlish C. Bangla Academy D. Muslim League Answer: B

Who declared at Dhaka University convocation in 1948 that 'Urdu and only Urdu shall be the state language of Pakistan'? A. Liaquat Ali Khan B. Mohammad Ali Jinnah C. Khawaja Nazimuddin D. Ayub Khan Answer: B
On which fateful date did student martyrs Salam, Barkat, Rafiq, and Jabbar lay down their lives for Bangla? A. 26 March 1971 B. 21 February 1952 C. 16 December 1971 D. 7 March 1971 Answer: B
In which year did UNESCO declare 21st February as International Mother Language Day? A. 1952 B. 1971 C. 1999 D. 2005 Answer: C
Who designed the original architectural concept of the Central Shaheed Minar in Dhaka? A. Zainul Abedin B. Hamidur Rahman C. Nitun Kundu D. Shamim Sikder Answer: B
Who was the renowned author of the poem and song 'Amar Bhaier Rokte Rangano Ekushey February'? A. Kazi Nazrul Islam B. Abdul Gaffar Choudhury C. Shamsur Rahman D. Altaf Mahmud Answer: B
Who composed the immortal melody of 'Amar Bhaier Rokte Rangano' sung today? A. Abdul Latif B. Altaf Mahmud C. Hemanta Mukherjee D. Sachin Dev Burman Answer: B
In which year did the Pakistan Constitution first officially recognize Bengali as a state language? A. 1952 B. 1954 C. 1956 D. 1962 Answer: C
What election symbol was used by the United Front (Jukta Front) in the 1954 East Bengal elections? A. Plough B. Boat (Nouka) C. Lantern D. Sheaf of paddy Answer: B
How many points constituted the electoral manifesto of the United Front in 1954? A. 6 points B. 11 points C. 21 points D. 14 points Answer: C
Who was appointed Chief Minister of East Bengal following the 1954 United Front victory? A. Huseyn Shaheed Suhrawardy B. A.K. Fazlul Huq (Sher-e-Bangla) C. Maulana Bhashani D. Nurul Amin Answer: B
When was the Awami Muslim League originally founded at Rose Garden in Dhaka? A. 14 August 1947 B. 23 June 1949 C. 21 February 1952 D. 7 March 1954 Answer: B
Who was the founding President of Awami Muslim League in 1949? A. Sheikh Mujibur Rahman B. Maulana Abdul Hamid Khan Bhashani C. Shamsul Haque D. Suhrawardy Answer: B
In which year was the word 'Muslim' dropped to transform the party into non-communal Awami League? A. 1952 B. 1955 C. 1958 D. 1966 Answer: B
General Ayub Khan imposed military rule (Martial Law) across Pakistan in: A. October 1958 B. March 1954 C. June 1960 D. January 1962 Answer: A
The historic 6-Point Charter of demands was presented by Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in: A. 1952 B. 1966 (Lahore) C. 1969 D. 1970 Answer: B
The 6-Point Charter is historically revered as the: A. Magna Carta of Bengali Emancipation B. Peace Treaty C. Cultural Manifesto D. Economic Accord Answer: A

What was the official name of the conspiracy case filed against Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and 34 others in 1968? A. Agartala Conspiracy Case B. Rawalpindi Case C. Lahore Trial D. Dhaka Sedition Case Answer: A

During the 1969 Mass Uprising, which university professor was brutally martyred in Rajshahi? A. Dr. Govinda Chandra Dev B. Dr. Mohammad Shamsuzzoha C. Dr. Jyotirmoy Guhathakurta D. Munier Choudhury Answer: B

The supreme honorific title 'Bangabandhu' (Friend of Bengal) was bestowed on Sheikh Mujib on: A. 7 March 1971 B. 23 February 1969 (Racecourse Ground by Tofail Ahmed) C. 26 March 1971 D. 10 January 1972 Answer: B

content.overview: 1970 General Elections landslide victory of Awami League, 7th March historic speech at Racecourse Ground, Operation Searchlight (25 March 1971), Declaration of Independence, Mujibnagar Government, Mukti Bahini, and Victory on 16 December 1971.
key_terms: 7 March 1971: 'The struggle this time is for our emancipation, the struggle this time is for our independence.'
Operation Searchlight: Genocidal crackdown launched by Pakistani military on the night of 25 March 1971.
study_notes: Mujibnagar Government took oath on 17 April 1971 at Baidyanathtala (Meherpur).
Sector Commander system divided Bangladesh into 11 military sectors.

mcqs.content: How many National Assembly seats out of 162 general seats in East Pakistan were won by Awami League in 1970? A. 100 B. 150 C. 160 D. 162 Answer: C
Where did Bangabandhu deliver his historic 7th March 1971 speech? A. Shahid Minar B. Racecourse Ground (now Suhrawardy Udyan) C. Paltan Maidan D. Dhaka University Answer: B
In which year was Bangabandhu's 7th March speech included in UNESCO's Memory of the World Register? A. 2011 B. 2015 C. 2017 D. 2020 Answer: C

What was the codename of the brutal military operation launched by the Pakistani army on 25 March 1971? A. Operation Blitz B. Operation Searchlight C. Operation Gibraltar D. Operation Clean-up Answer: B
When did Bangabandhu declare the Independence of Bangladesh? A. 7 March 1971 B. Early hours of 26 March 1971 (before arrest) C. 17 April 1971 D. 16 December 1971 Answer: B
On which date did the provisional government of Bangladesh (Mujibnagar Government) formally take oath? A. 26 March 1971 B. 10 April 1971 C. 17 April 1971 (Meherpur) D. 16 December 1971 Answer: C
Who was the President of the provisional Mujibnagar Government? A. Syed Nazrul Islam B. Tajuddin Ahmad C. Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman (in absentia) D. M.A.G. Osmani Answer: C
Who served as the Acting President of the Mujibnagar Government during 1971? A. Tajuddin Ahmad B. Syed Nazrul Islam C. Khondaker Mostaq D. Mansur Ali Answer: B
Who was the Prime Minister of the wartime Mujibnagar Government? A. Tajuddin Ahmad B. Syed Nazrul Islam C. A.H.M. Qamaruzzaman D. M.A.G. Osmani Answer: A
Who served as the Commander-in-Chief of the Mukti Bahini (Liberation Forces) during 1971? A. Major Ziaur Rahman B. General M.A.G. Osmani C. Major K.M. Shafiullah D. Major Khaled Mosharraf Answer: B
Into how many operational military sectors was Bangladesh divided during the Liberation War? A. 7 sectors B. 9 sectors C. 11 sectors D. 14 sectors Answer: C
Which sector was unique in having no designated permanent sector commander (naval commando operations)? A. Sector 1 B. Sector 5 C. Sector 10 D. Sector 11 Answer: C
What was the highest military gallantry award conferred by Bangladesh for supreme bravery in 1971? A. Bir Bikrom B. Bir Uttam C. Bir Sreshtho D. Bir Protik Answer: C
How many heroic freedom fighters were awarded the title 'Bir Sreshtho'? A. 5 B. 7 C. 11 D. 14 Answer: B
Which radio station operated as the voice of inspiration for freedom fighters during 1971? A. Radio Pakistan B. Swadhin Bangla Betar Kendra C. Voice of America D. BBC Bangla Answer: B
The Concert for Bangladesh to aid refugees was organized at Madison Square Garden by George Harrison and: A. Pandit Ravi Shankar B. Bob Dylan C. Eric Clapton D. John Lennon Answer: A
Which date is commemorated across Bangladesh as Martyred Intellectuals Day (Buddhijibi Dibosh)? A. 25 March B. 7 March C. 14 December D. 16 December Answer: C
On which historic date did 93,000 Pakistani troops surrender unconditionally, bringing victory? A. 26 March 1971 B. 14 December 1971 C. 16 December 1971 D. 10 January 1972 Answer: C

Where was the Instrument of Surrender signed between General Niazi and General Jagjit Singh Aurora on 16 Dec 1971? A. Dhaka Cantonment B. Racecourse Ground (Dhaka) C. Bangabhaban D. Lalbagh Fort Answer: B
On which date did Father of the Nation Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman return home to independent Bangladesh? A. 16 December 1971 B. 26 March 1972 C. 10 January 1972 D. 17 April 1972 Answer: C
